newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mixed outlook for S.African building sector.
newsitem.headline: Mixed outlook for S.African building sector.

text.p: The residential and non-residential building sector's outlook was bleak, but the civil engineering construction sector should get a boost, the University of Stellenbosch's Bureau for Economic Research(BER) said on Monday.

"The short-term prospects for the building industry are not particularly rosey, and the overall level of building activity is likely to deteriorate further in the third quarter of this year," BER said in its latest survey of the sector.

But the civil engineering construction sector should benefit from an uptick in the national road building programme, mainly for toll roads, and the Infrastructure Corporation of South Africa's increased funding of municipal projects.
"Work volumes in the industry are likely to rise in the year ahead," BER said.
Possible interest rate cuts could lead to increased building activity but would likely benefit the private residential sector sooner than the non-residential market.
Second-quarter building cost increases continued to decelerate, expected to rise by an average eight percent for the year compared to the previously forecast 9.1 percent.
Architects and quantity surveyors reported the number of contracts awarded fell in the second quarter, forcing many to cut back on employees. But no major change was expected in the third quarter.
BER said it remained cheaper to buy houses than build them because the townhouse market was increasingly overstocked in some areas.
Non-residential building activity in the first four months of the year was up from year ago levels but was expected to level off in the third quarter.
